transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm just having some trouble at work. I work at a front desk, and... well, lately, if a door slams, or someone rolls a suitcase fast across the lobby, I just... I jump. Like it's happening again. 

It takes me a minute to get my heart rate back down. So... that's what really pushed me to come in.
What do you mean by 'it's happening again'?
Well... there was an incident. About two weeks ago. A guest got upset and... he threatened me. At the front desk. So... yeah. It's just been going on since then.
Do you ever find yourself reliving that incident at the front desk?

Yeah... I guess. Just... out of nowhere, sometimes. 

I could just be trying to answer a normal phone call, and... I'll get this picture in my head. Of him leaning over the counter, knocking the equipment toward me. It just... pops up.
Have you been avoiding anything because it reminds you of what happened at the front desk?

Um... yeah. A little bit. 

I've been... I guess I take the back hallway now, whenever I can. Just... walking past that spot in the lobby, it makes my chest feel tight. So I just... I try to stay away from it.
Have you been having trouble sleeping since the incident at the front desk?
Um... no. Not really. I've been sleeping okay, I guess.
Do you have difficulty concentrating?

Yeah... I suppose so. 

At the desk, I used to move through the reservations pretty smoothly. But lately... I don't know. I just keep rereading the same screen. And... second-guessing really simple things, like which room note to enter first. Just... stuff like that.
Do you find yourself startling easily in situations that wouldn't have bothered you before the incident?

Um... yeah. I guess so. That's... actually what pushed me to come in. 

Just... if a door slams, or... someone rolls a suitcase fast across the lobby... I jump. Like it's happening again. And... I don't know, it just takes me a minute to get my heart to settle down. So... yeah.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms since the incident at the front desk?
Um... about two weeks, I guess. Just... ever since that guest threatened me. Since then.
Are there any people or situations that you've been avoiding since the incident at the front desk?

Well... yeah. I guess. 

I just... I've been taking the back hallway lately. Whenever I can, anyway. Walking past that spot in the lobby... I don't know, my chest just gets really tight. I just... I just want to get away from it. So I don't go out there much.
Do you find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential threats or dangers in your daily life?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think I do that. I just... I haven't noticed anything like that, anyway.
Do you feel guilty or responsible in any way for what happened with the guest at the front desk?
No... I mean, I was just doing my job. It wasn't my fault he started acting like that. So... no. I don't think I feel guilty.
Have you avoided talking or thinking about the incident at the front desk?
Um... no, not really. I mean, it still crosses my mind sometimes. And I've had to talk about it a little bit with my manager, so... no. I wouldn't say I'm avoiding it.
{"intent": "Determine the presence of hypervigilance", "question": "Do you often feel like you're "on edge" or constantly waiting for something to happen?"}
I don't... I wouldn't say that. I just feel pretty normal, mostly. I'm not sitting around waiting for things to happen.
Has what happened at the front desk caused problems in your relationships or daily activities outside of work?

Um... outside of work? No, not really. I mean, I'm still showing up to my job and everything. 

Though... my manager did have to shorten a couple of my shifts recently. I guess I've been a little slower at the reservation desk lately. And... I kind of keep finding excuses not to cross the lobby when guests need help. But other than that... no. Things are fine.
Have you avoided social interactions or activities you normally enjoy because of what happened at the front desk?
No, not really. I still do the same stuff I usually do. I haven't stopped seeing anyone or... changed what I do on my days off. It's just normal.
Have you felt like what happened at the front desk has significantly impacted your overall well-being or daily life?

I mean... like I said before, I'm still showing up to work. It's just... my manager did cut a few of my shifts short. I've been a bit slow at the desk, I guess. And... I just don't really want to walk across the lobby right now, so I try not to. But... I don't know if that's a huge deal.
Have you avoided other places or situations outside of work because they remind you of the incident at the front desk?
No... not really. Like I said, outside of work is fine. I don't think I've avoided anywhere else.
Have you been avoiding talking to people in general because of what happened at the front desk?
No... I don't think so. I mean, I still talk to people. It's just... normal conversations. I haven't really been avoiding anyone specifically.
